text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as oil prices held near elevated levels, though the move was modest. Over the past two weeks, the stock has climbed 12.8%—a much larger gain—driven by a sharp spike in crude prices triggered by escalating attacks on oil infrastructure in the Middle East. Houthi militants claimed strikes on Saudi Arabian airports and Aramco facilities on October 19th, and shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have intensified, pushing Brent crude above $109 per barrel and widening the gap between world oil prices ($126.55) and U.S. oil ($101.91).

The company benefits directly when crude prices rise, since higher oil prices translate to stronger revenues and profits for major producers. While today's small gain suggests the immediate geopolitical shock has started to fade—news from October 20th mentions hopes for diplomatic progress in the Middle East—the stock remains well above where it started two weeks ago, reflecting the underlying strength in energy prices from ongoing regional tensions.
